target_customer: Small and mid-size retailers who want to accept mobile payments without card fees
problem: Card interchange costs retailers 2 to 5 percent per transaction. Kash cleared payments directly through bank debit with no card network.
business_model: Payments processing fees on direct bank debit, plus POS software and a B2B payments API
product_category: Mobile payments and direct bank debit

founders.name: Kaz Nejatian
founders.background_notes: Named CEO and co-founder in TechCrunch and the Green Visor release. The company began in Canada before moving to San Francisco for YC. No background found in an opened source.

founders.name: Geoff Flarity
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder and COO on the YC page; no background given.

competitors.name: Square
competitors.what: Card payments and merchant tools for small retailers

competitors.name: Credit card networks and processors
competitors.what: Incumbent card rails with interchange fees and slower settlement

technical_complexity.rationale: Moving money by direct bank debit with chargeback guarantees means integrating bank rails, risk handling and a mobile and POS stack.

defensibility.rationale: Two-sided retailer and consumer network was early; banks, Apple Pay and other mobile wallets could offer similar low-fee flows.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Press says Kash was acquired around 2017 but the acquirer is not named in sources found.

market_need_then: Retailers paid 2 to 5 percent in card fees per the company. In July 2014 TechCrunch reported dozens of beta retailers in the Bay Area, with 15 to 20 percent of their customers trying Kash.

branding.domain_note: Used withkash.com, a prefix variant, per the YC page; no purchase story found.

identity.visual_style: App showed a green debit card with a tap to pay prompt per PYMNTS.
identity.voice_and_tone: YC tagline: We are fixing how money works.

brand_strength.rationale: Modest press coverage in 2014 and 2015; the name resembles Cash App and bKash, which cluttered brand searches.

pivots.from: Consumer and retailer mobile payment app
pivots.to: liveACH B2B payments API and Kash Register POS
pivots.why: Not stated; American Banker described the product set in September 2015.

outcome_analysis: Kash started in Canada, joined YC in summer 2014, and raised about 2 million dollars from Draper Associates, Green Visor and Structure Capital, then a Green Visor led seed in 2015. Its offering widened to a B2B payments API and POS. It is listed as acquired, around 2017 per secondary sources, but the buyer and price are not public.
notes: withkash.com did not resolve in this session; treated as unreachable. The 2 million dollar seed is from the company's Medium post (title seen in search; page returned 403) and FinSMEs; the 2015 round amount is undisclosed. Acquirer and the 2017 date come only from Seedtable and a CB Insights bio, so unverified. One CB Insights page claims a Block subsidiary link, unverified. Other founder names (Danny Su) appear only on Seedtable.
